Pediatric Heart Network echocardiographic z-scores

Source: R/phn_zscore.R
phn_zscore.Rd

Computes body-surface-area-adjusted z-scores for pediatric echocardiographic measurements from the Pediatric Heart Network (PHN) Normal Echocardiogram Database (Lopez et al., 2017), and the normal (z = 0) value for each child's BSA.

The PHN model indexes each measurement X to BSA raised to a structure-specific power alpha, and the indexed value is normally distributed with no residual dependence on BSA. So

z = (X / BSA^alpha - mean) / sd

with alpha, mean and sd from the paper's Table 2 (see phn_zscore_table()). The predicted normal value is mean * BSA^alpha. For the three ratios (LVMTV, LVTTD, LVSI) alpha is 0, so BSA does not change their z-scores, though it must still be given, and a missing BSA gives NA.

Usage

phn_zscore(x, structure, units, bsa = NULL, height_cm = NULL, weight_kg = NULL)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector of measurements.

structure

Character, the paper's abbreviation for the structure measured (for example "ANN"); length 1, or the length of x.

units

Character, the unit x is in (for example "mm"); length 1, or the length of x. Required; see Details.

bsa

Numeric vector of body surface area in m^2, length 1 or the length of x. Give this or height_cm and weight_kg.

height_cm, weight_kg

Numeric vectors of height in cm and weight in kg at the echocardiogram, length 1 or the length of x, used to compute BSA by bsa_haycock().

Value

A data.frame with one row per element of x and columns structure, x, units, bsa (m^2), predicted (the normal value for that BSA, in units), and z. z is NA where x or BSA is NA; predicted does not depend on x, and is NA where BSA is NA. Both are NA for a missing BSA even for the ratios, whose z-scores do not otherwise depend on BSA.

Details

BSA. Give bsa directly, or height_cm and weight_kg, from which BSA is computed with the Haycock formula (bsa_haycock()), the formula the PHN used. Not both. Use the height and weight measured at the echocardiogram: z-scores computed from birth weight and length are not z-scores for the child that was imaged.

Units. units is required, so that a measurement recorded in mm is never scored against a norm in cm. Linear structures accept "mm" or "cm", areas "mm2" or "cm2"; volumes must be "ml", mass "g", LVMTV "g/ml" and LVTTD and LVSI "none". The coronary arteries are tabulated in mm in the paper, the other linear structures in cm; either unit works for both.

Structures. structure takes the paper's abbreviations, listed with their definitions by phn_zscore_table(). Among them: aortic annulus ANN, aortic root ROOT, sinotubular junction STJ, ascending aorta AAO, pulmonary annulus PVSAX (short axis) and PVLAX (long axis), main and branch pulmonary arteries MPA, RPA, LPA, mitral and tricuspid diameters MVAP, MVLAT, TVAP, TVLAT, and the LV dimensions LVEDD, LVPWT, LVST. Matching ignores case.

The paper defines ROOT only as "aortic root diameter", measured in the parasternal long axis (Table 2); the ParameterZ PHN calculator labels it "Sinus of Valsalva". LVEDA is the LV short-axis end-diastolic area (cm^2); it is not interchangeable with LVEDD, the end-diastolic diameter, nor with an LV area traced in an apical view.

Views and derived quantities. A z-score is only as comparable as the measurement behind it, so match the view: the view column of phn_zscore_table() gives Table 2's view for each structure. Several structures were not measured directly but computed from others, and should be scored only when computed the same way:

  • MVA and TVA, the valve areas, are ellipses from the two annular diameters, pi/4 * AP * LAT, not planimetered areas.

  • LVEDV and LVEDVEPI are 5/6 * area * length (the bullet formula).

  • LVM is 1.05 * (LVEDVEPI - LVEDV).

  • The ratios are LVMTV = LVM / LVEDV, LVTTD = LVPWT / LVEDD and LVSI = LVEDL / LVEDD.

What the model does not include. The paper found age, sex and race effects that were statistically significant but under 5% in size, and so clinically insignificant; the published z-score uses the single mean and SD in Table 2, as here. The reference population is healthy, non-obese children aged 0 to 18 years. Its exclusions (Data Supplement, Table 1) include structural heart disease and a corrected gestational age under 37 weeks at enrollment, so a premature infant is scored against term norms.

References

Lopez L, Colan S, Stylianou M, et al. Relationship of echocardiographic Z scores adjusted for body surface area to age, sex, race, and ethnicity: the Pediatric Heart Network Normal Echocardiogram Database. Circ Cardiovasc Imaging. 2017;10(11):e006979. doi:10.1161/CIRCIMAGING.117.006979 . Coefficients: Table 2. Z-score formula and worked example: Results, after Table 2.

Haycock GB, Schwartz GJ, Wisotsky DH. Geometric method for measuring body surface area: a height-weight formula validated in infants, children, and adults. J Pediatr. 1978;93(1):62-66. doi:10.1016/s0022-3476(78)80601-5

See also

phn_zscore_table(), bsa_haycock()

Examples

# The paper's worked example: a mitral diameter of 11 mm at BSA 0.3 m^2
phn_zscore(11, "MVLAT", units = "mm", bsa = 0.3)
#>   structure  x units bsa predicted         z
#> 1     MVLAT 11    mm 0.3  12.21421 -1.007654

# Aortic annulus from height and weight at the echo
phn_zscore(c(7.5, 9, 12), "ANN", units = "mm",
           height_cm = c(52, 60, 75), weight_kg = c(3.8, 5.6, 9.4))
#>   structure    x units       bsa predicted         z
#> 1       ANN  7.5    mm 0.2382383  7.223830 0.4041496
#> 2       ANN  9.0    mm 0.3106097  8.248390 0.9632896
#> 3       ANN 12.0    mm 0.4483351  9.909759 2.2298055
